source: generic ticagrelor has been on the US market since 2025-05-01, so no label change this academic study could win would earn AstraZeneca anything. FDA Paragraph IV list for NDA 22433 (Brilinta 90 mg): first approval 2018-09-04, first marketing 2025-05-01; openFDA Drugs@FDA holds 19 ticagrelor ANDAs, among them Apotex ANDA208584 (2025-05-01), Alembic ANDA208576 (2025-05-02) and InvaGen ANDA208537 (2025-05-05), marketing status Prescription (queried 2026-11-16). AstraZeneca's own words: Brilinta US revenue for the nine months to 2026-09-30 was $16m, down 95%, 'Decline driven by generic entry in the US and Europe in Q2 2025' (Q3 2026 results, 6-K 0001654954-26-009256, filed 2026-10-30). NCT05047172 (CAPTIVA) is sponsored by the University of Florida and funded by NINDS (U01NS117450), AstraZeneca and Janssen are collaborators, and ticagrelor plus aspirin is one of two experimental arms against clopidogrel plus aspirin (registry, checked 2026-11-16)
note: the only Brilinta patent left in the Orange Book, 10300065 to 2036-01-27, carries use codes U-2541 and U-2542, both 60 mg twice daily after MI or ACS; nothing protects a stroke or intracranial use.
